ext.description: A deep-learning study buddy for PyTorch/TensorFlow: shows tensor shape errors before you run, and explains in plain words why training is not working
cfg.level: Explanation level. Beginner uses very plain words; Normal uses more precise terms.
cfg.autoRecord: Record settings and results of every `deepfriend.watch()` run into the project's `.deepfriend/` folder (never uploaded).
cfg.ai.provider: AI used to polish explanation sentences. Decisions are always made by fixed rules; AI only rewrites wording. All core features work without AI.
cfg.ai.provider.vscode: AI built into VS Code (e.g. Copilot, no key needed)
cfg.ai.provider.openai: OpenAI-compatible endpoint (OpenAI, Gemini, Ollama…, your API key)
cfg.ai.consent: Whether to ask before sending error text or code snippets to the AI.
cfg.ai.consent.ask: Show what will be sent and ask each time
cfg.ai.openaiBaseUrl: OpenAI-compatible API base URL, e.g. https://api.openai.com/v1 or http://localhost:11434/v1
cfg.ai.openaiModel: Model name for the OpenAI-compatible API.
cfg.shapeHints: Show tensor shapes (e.g. → (32, 64, 112, 112)) in grey at the end of layer lines.
cfg.runtimeCheck: If PyTorch is installed, double-check shapes with fake 'meta' tensors that compute sizes only. Your training script is never run.
cfg.pythonPath: Path of the Python executable DeepFriend should use. Leave empty to detect automatically.
cfg.errorReporting: Show a 'Report on GitHub' button when DeepFriend itself fails. Nothing is sent automatically; you review and submit it yourself.
